meta.title: For parents
meta.description: A clear view of lesson goals, homework, tutor feedback, attendance, and learning progress.

hero.title: Know what your child is learning, and what comes next.
hero.body: See lesson goals, homework, tutor feedback, attendance, and progress in one clear parent workspace.
hero.reassurance: You stay involved in the important decisions while the tutor manages the day-to-day learning.
hero.note: No long forms. We start with a short conversation about your child's needs.

dashboard.label: Illustrative parent workspace
dashboard.subject: Mathematics · Grade 6
dashboard.feedbackValue: Aram understands equivalent fractions visually. Next, we will practise common denominators.
dashboard.illustrative: Example content. Your workspace reflects your child's actual plan and lessons.

visibility.title: Everything important, in one place
visibility.body: Open the part you need without piecing together updates from messages, calendars, and homework links.

tabs.label: Overview
tabs.title: A useful snapshot, not a wall of data
tabs.body: See the next class, active learning goal, homework status, and latest tutor note together.

tabs.label: Feedback
tabs.title: Specific notes after the lesson
tabs.body: Review the topic covered, participation, strengths, challenges, recommendation, and next focus.

tabs.label: Homework
tabs.title: One place to follow assigned work
tabs.body: Parents have read-only visibility into the task, due date, submission, tutor review, and grade when used.

tabs.label: Progress
tabs.title: Evidence behind the learning plan
tabs.body: Follow current goals, milestones, assessment evidence, and tutor observations over time.

tabs.label: Schedule
tabs.title: Classes and attendance at a glance
tabs.body: See upcoming lessons, attendance, reschedules, cancellations, and the time zone used for planning.

lesson.title: What parents receive after each lesson
lesson.body: Feedback is structured to explain what happened and guide the next class, not to provide generic praise.
lesson.next: Practise three scaffolded examples before moving to word problems.
lesson.planAction: Learning plan update requires parent acknowledgment

plan.title: A clear path, not disconnected lessons
plan.body: The active plan brings together the student's current level, short- and long-term goals, priority skills, planned sequence, review points, and evidence of progress.

level.title: We start from the student's actual level
level.body: School grade is useful context, but it is not the whole picture. The starting point can combine a parent consultation, school topics, student work, a placement assessment when useful, tutor observation, and previous results.

pathways.title: Catching up
pathways.body: Build prerequisite skills before returning to current coursework.

pathways.title: Staying on track
pathways.body: Reinforce school learning, practise consistently, and address gaps early.

pathways.title: Moving ahead
pathways.body: Introduce more advanced material when the evidence shows the student is ready.

level.note: The learning plan can change as new evidence appears.

tutor.title: Tutors are reviewed for subject fit and teaching readiness
tutor.body: 2tor keeps internal verification records for identity, education or certification, background checks where used, references, safeguarding, platform onboarding, and subject-specific preparation. A tutor's public profile shows teaching capabilities without exposing private documents.
tutor.name: Mariam S.
tutor.approach: Uses visual models first, then moves to symbolic practice and explanation.

communication.title: Clear communication without constant messaging
communication.body: Parents should not need to ask after every class what happened. The essential information is recorded in lesson feedback, with parent-inclusive messaging for questions and changes.
communication.tutorMessage: Today we focused on fraction comparison. Aram improved with visual models but still needs practice explaining why two fractions are equivalent.
communication.parentMessage: Thank you. Please keep the next homework short because of school exams this week.
communication.note: Messages are part of a parent-inclusive learning space. Response timing depends on tutor and support availability.

control.title: You stay in control of important decisions
control.body: The tutor leads instruction. Parents keep visibility and control over enrollment, major plan changes, privacy, schedule decisions, payments, and requests to change tutor.

formats.title: Choose the format that fits your child
formats.body: Neither option is automatically better. The useful choice depends on the learning need, pace, timing, and available compatible learners.

group.title: Group lessons
group.note: Group availability depends on finding compatible learners.

safety.title: Designed around student privacy
safety.body: Student accounts are linked to parents, learning records are relationship-scoped, and student-visible conversations must include a parent or guardian. Uploaded learning files are kept private, scanned, and shared through short-lived authorized links.

beforeAfter.title: You should not have to become the tutor
beforeAfter.body: Stay close to the decisions that matter without rebuilding the learning record yourself.
without: Asking what happened after every class
Repeating instructions between tutor and child
Tracking lessons in messages and spreadsheets

start.title: Getting started is simple
start.body: A short conversation creates a sensible starting point. You can review the recommendation before deciding what happens next.

steps.title: Tell us what you are noticing
steps.body: Share the current school level, difficult topics, goals, and schedule.

steps.title: We identify the right starting point
steps.body: We use the consultation, and an assessment or tutor review when useful.

steps.title: Meet the tutor
steps.body: Confirm the tutor, subject, lesson format, schedule, and pricing before lessons begin.

steps.title: Track the learning
steps.body: Receive lesson feedback and follow goals, homework, attendance, and milestones.

form.title: Tell us about your child
form.body: It takes about two minutes. We only ask for the information needed to start a useful conversation.

form.subject: Subject

faq.title: Direct answers before you decide
items: How often will I receive feedback?
Published lesson feedback is available after each completed lesson.
Can I see what my child is learning?
Yes. Linked parents can view the active learning plan, goals, milestones, parent-visible feedback, and assigned work.
Can I communicate directly with the tutor?
Parent-inclusive conversations support progress questions, homework concerns, and schedule updates. The platform does not create private adult-child channels.
Progress is connected to goals and milestones supported by evidence such as tutor observations, assignments, projects, or assessments.
A linked parent can submit a tutor-change request. The support team reviews the request and manages the matching process.
Can we switch between individual and group lessons?
You can discuss a format change with the team. Group placement depends on compatible learners and availability.
What if my child falls behind?
The tutor can revisit prerequisite skills and recommend a learning-plan adjustment based on new evidence.
What if my child needs more advanced material?
The plan can move ahead when tutor observation and learning evidence show the student is ready.
Tutors assign and review work in the platform. Linked parents have read-only visibility into assignments, submissions, grades, and files.
Are lessons aligned with school curriculum?
School topics can inform the plan, while the tutor also addresses prerequisites and individual goals. Alignment depends on the subject and the plan you agree on.
2tor maintains internal records for identity and relevant education, certification, training, and other review types. Public profiles show approved teaching capabilities, not private documents.
Linked parents can see relationship-scoped learning records, including parent-visible feedback, plans, assignments, schedule information, and milestones.
Contact support to discuss pausing or ending lessons and any schedule or payment implications.
What happens during the free consultation?
We discuss the learner's current context, goals, schedule, possible starting point, tutor fit, lesson format, and pricing. You can decide what to do next.

final.title: See the learning clearly.
final.body: Tell us what your child needs. We will help you understand a sensible starting point, tutor, and lesson format.
final.note: No pressure. Start with a short conversation.
